summary: Specifies a simple mode of sending fax data over Internet mail, using standard email transport and a defined image format. It is a standards-track document and was replaced by RFC 3965.

eli5.summary: Sending a fax as a normal email with a picture of the page attached, instead of using a phone line.

questions: how to send fax over email
subtitle: Sending fax documents over Internet mail using TIFF format.

tldr.problem: Fax machines on telephone networks cannot easily communicate with computers on the Internet, and people want to send fax documents using email.
tldr.mechanism: IFax devices and gateways use standard Internet mail protocols (SMTP, MIME) and TIFF for Facsimile (an image format) to send, receive, and forward fax documents. An offramp gateway translates from Internet mail to phone-line fax for delivery to traditional fax machines.
tldr.outcome: Computers and fax devices can exchange documents through a common email system; existing email software works without modification, and the format is compatible with standard fax operation.

today: RFC 2305 is a Proposed Standard and has been obsoleted by RFC 3965, which provides updated specifications for Internet fax.

sections.title: Bridges Between Fax and Email
sections.content:
Facsimile (fax) machines use the telephone network to send and receive documents. Internet mail is a separate system that works over the Internet. This RFC creates a "simple mode" profile that lets the two systems interoperate.

The design is deliberately profile-based rather than a new protocol: it reuses standard Internet mail (RFC 821, RFC 822), MIME (RFC 2049), and TIFF for Facsimile (an image format), so that existing email clients can read and send faxes without modification. A G3Fax device is a traditional fax machine using the ITU-T T.4 standard and the general switched telephone network (GSTN). An IFax device is an Internet-accessible device that can send, receive, or forward faxes using Internet mail. An offramp gateway translates from Internet mail to phone-line fax, while an onramp gateway translates from phone-line fax to Internet mail.
sections.eli5: The system lets you send a fax from your computer, and lets someone with only a fax machine receive it printed out, using the Internet and phone systems together.

sections.title: Communication Paths and Device Types
sections.content:
The RFC describes five communication scenarios:

  • Internet mail to a network printer that acts as an IFax device.
  • Internet mail through an offramp gateway to a traditional G3Fax device.
  • A network scanner as an IFax device sending to a network printer.
  • A network scanner sending through an offramp gateway to a G3Fax device.
  • A network scanner sending to Internet mail.

Transport between IFax devices uses standard Internet mail transfer mechanisms. The format of addresses must conform to RFC 821 (the <addr-spec> field) and RFC 822 (the <mailbox> field). An offramp gateway that serves multiple users should use SMTP; one serving a single recipient may use POP or IMAP to access a mailbox.
sections.eli5: Different devices can talk to each other: computers to printers, computers to fax machines (through a gateway), scanners to printers, etc., all via email.

sections.title: Image Format and Message Structure
sections.content:
Facsimile images are encoded in TIFF for Facsimile format (also called the S profile), defined in ITU-T standards and RFC 2301. MIME carries the image as the image/TIFF media type. IFax devices MUST be able to read and write the minimum set of TIFF fields defined by the S profile; they SHOULD not use optional TIFF fields unless they have prior knowledge that the recipient supports them.

IFax messages MUST comply with MIME (RFC 2049) and RFC 822 message header formatting. The MIME structure allows single multi-page documents to be sent as a single TIFF file (recommended) or as multiple TIFF files in a multipart message. If processing of any part fails, the entire message is treated as failing. Messages sent via SMTP MUST include a MAIL FROM address appropriate for bounce notification, as specified in the Delivery Status Notification protocol.
sections.eli5: Fax images are stored in a standard picture format (TIFF), wrapped in a regular email message that any email program understands.

sections.title: Email and Telephone Addresses
sections.content:
Messages to normal Internet mail recipients use standard email addresses without constraints. For G3Fax devices, the recipient's telephone number must be encoded in an Internet mail address and supplied to the offramp gateway. The address MUST be contained in standard SMTP transport fields such as RCPT TO and MAIL FROM. The telephone number format SHOULD conform to RFC 2303 or RFC 2304; other formats MUST be syntactically distinct so that gateways can distinguish them.

As with all Internet mail addresses, the left-hand portion of an address is interpreted only by the MTA named on the right-hand side (the domain part). This allows offramp gateways serving multiple G3Fax users to route mail based on the transport envelope rather than message content headers.
sections.eli5: To send to a fax machine, you write its phone number as if it were an email address on the gateway system (like fax-number@gateway.example.com).

sections.title: Threats and Protections
sections.content:
Internet fax adds security concerns beyond those of Internet mail or traditional fax. A spoofed sender can forge the From or MAIL FROM fields; encryption-based authentication (S/MIME or PGP/MIME) can address this. Offramp gateways must authorize senders to prevent unauthorized and costly dial-outs to G3Fax numbers. Confidential information such as calling card numbers encoded in destination addresses may be disclosed on the cover page; senders need methods to prevent this disclosure.

G3Fax recipients must be provided with sufficient information to trace the originator (such as MAIL FROM, From, Sender, Reply-To, Message-ID, and Received headers), as many jurisdictions legally require the sender to be identified on a faxed document. Traditional fax users expect higher privacy than typical Internet email; encryption (either via VPN/IPSec for channel security or via S/MIME/PGP for object security) can preserve this expectation. Bounces (delivery failures) may be sent to unmonitored accounts or printers, creating a traffic analysis risk.
sections.eli5: Fax machines are used for important documents, so the system must prevent people from sending fake faxes, stop bad actors from making expensive phone calls, and keep secrets from leaking.
